data.content_ref: inline:Acyclic-defense suspension refinement: after the grounded fixpoint, run a second deterministic pure-function pass that marks each IN node as either acyclic-defended (every defense path terminates in an unattacked IN node) or cycle-dependent (IN-ness essentially depends on a cycle). Committed roots that are cycle-dependent are flagged 'suspended (cycle-dependent)' at the commitment layer only — the base IN label is preserved, so Pass 1 determinism and the least-fixpoint characterization are untouched. This adds a conservative distinction the Dung semantics deliberately flattens, and gives the scheduler a principled reason to withhold commitment until an exogenous anchor breaks the cycle.
